newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's central Prairies saw frost, little rain.
newsitem.headline: Canada's central Prairies saw frost, little rain.

text.p: Canada's central Prairies Friday saw overnight lows of -4 Celsius (24.8 F) in central and southeast Saskatchewan where 53 percent of harvest was complete and only trace amounts of rain fell in Alberta, Environment Canada said.

Alberta's northern Peace River Valley also saw overnight lows of -2 Celsius (28.4 F) and western Manitoba's Brandon, Dauphin and Swan River regions saw below freezing temperatures, a meteorologist said.
Only Alberta saw trace amounts of rain while the rest of the Prairies saw clear skies overnight.
Harvest was stalled for one to three weeks on wet weather.
Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete, Saskatchewan combined 53 percent of crops and Manitoba had 75 percent of crops in the bin by Sept 30, provincial crop reports said.
Alberta was forecast to see clearing skies with highs of 13 to 22 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see a mainly sunny skies with highs of 13 to 22 Celsius.
Manitoba was forecast to see mainly sunny skies with highs of 11 to 16 Celsius.
